item.title: 'I hold children who will probably not survive because of the cuts I'm forced to make', says UN aid chief UN
item.description: UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher has warned of worsening conditions in conflict zones, describing places such as Sudan and Gaza as an “atrocities lab”, where new weapons are being developed and tested amid devastating human suffering.

item.title: Body horror and 'Becoming America': The best things to do, hear, see or watch in Europe this week
item.description: Chris Pratt returns for season 2 of Prime's gritty Reacher follow-up, 'The Terminal List', while Tom Rhys Harries brings body horror to the DC Universe in 'Clayface'. Here's what to look out for this week.

item.title: Greek authorities say 12 migrants die in two incidents in Aegean Sea
item.description: At least 1,209 migrants have died or gone missing in the Mediterranean since the beginning of the year, according to the International Organisation for Migration.

item.title: How much does inflation cost you? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot
item.description: Across Europe, people are protesting rising housing, food, and energy costs, demanding government action. But how is rising inflation hitting Europeans' daily lives? Ask the Euronews AI chatbot.

item.title: Marco Rubio denies there was any pause in US intelligence sharing with Ukraine
item.description: Meanwhile, Ukraine is pushing ahead with plans to develop European alternatives to US-made air defence systems and Starlink satellite communications, with discussions already under way.

item.title: Place de la République flares again as Macron admits intelligence failures
item.description: Nearly 2,400 people were arrested and almost 1,000 officers injured in a single day of nationwide unrest over the cost of living, leaving Paris shopkeepers sweeping up and bracing for more.

item.title: France grapples with the aftermath of a weekend of violence
item.description: Hello from Brussels. It’s Monday, and I’m Mared Gwyn. Today: France grapples with the aftermath of a weekend of violence and chaos, and Trump berates Zelenskyy once again.

item.title: Europe Today: France counts cost of violence as Ukraine hits St Petersburg, Leningrad
item.description: France is cleaning up after the worst unrest in years, as violent groups hijacked the marches. Also on today's Europe Today: Ukraine hits St. Petersburg in a large-scale drone attack, and the UN’s aid chief, Tom Fletcher, warns that more aid workers are at risk of dying.

item.title: Albanian police clash with protesters in Tirana as unrest enters sixth day
item.description: Albanian police used water cannon and tear gas in Tirana as anti-government protests over university conditions and corruption turned violent.

item.title: Albertans vote on path to independence as Carney fights to keep Canada united
item.description: Alberta has the world's fourth-largest proven oil reserves and separatist momentum has been driven by anger over Ottawa's management of the sector.

item.title: More than 200 arrested in second day of street clashes against cost of living in Milan
item.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called for a security meeting on Monday to address the violence, which resembled some scenes of chaos and looting in Paris.

item.title: Leatherback turtles are declining rapidly. Could a network of ‘ocean sanctuaries’ save them?
item.description: Experts warn that it could take 265 years to reach a crucial target to protect 30 per cent of the ocean under the current rate of progress.

item.title: How a $5 billion ‘Gas Ring’ could strengthen Central Asia’s energy security
item.description: A proposed $5bn (€4.45bn) gas network could help five Central Asian countries share supplies and meet winter demand. The ‘Gas Ring’ would link new and existing pipelines, but funding and agreements between governments remain to be finalised.

item.title: Why 2027 is set to be the year for birdwatching holidays – and where to go birding in Europe
item.description: We’re now heading into the ‘birdwatching era’ with a new generation picking up the binoculars and travelling for birding holidays.

item.title: Wages vs prices: The economic pressures behind Europe's protests
item.description: From rising food prices and unaffordable housing to stagnant purchasing power and strained public services, demonstrations across Europe highlight growing frustration over living standards.

item.title: China’s economy grows 4.5% on robust exports as domestic weakness persists
item.description: The official growth figure from the July-September quarter beat expectations and picked up from 4.3% in April-June, the slowest pace in more than three years.

item.title: Can Spain afford its pensions? What to know about the funding debate ahead of the election
item.description: Spain’s pension system is not bankrupt, but increasingly relies on state funding. Social Security ended 2025 with a deficit of 0.4% of GDP after €47.8 billion in state transfers. Research institute Fedea puts the underlying deficit, excluding those transfers, at 4.15% of GDP.

item.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu nine days before Israeli election, breaking months of silence
item.description: Trump's late backing comes as the two leaders’ strategies on Iran and Gaza have diverged, and he warns the US may not “do this work” if Israel changes leaders.

item.title: Macron vows to hold those who sought to 'bring down the Republic' accountable after riots
item.description: Macron vowed to hold rioters accountable after violent scenes of looting and rioting across France, with unrest deepening political tensions ahead of next year’s presidential election.

item.title: Tensions remain high in Paris after violent protests across France
item.description: Small gatherings and isolated fires were reported at several locations in Paris on Sunday, a day after violent protests in other French cities.

item.title: Spain changes Ceuta patrol rules over ships' "innocent passage"
item.description: The Spanish Navy has changed its protocol in response to the innocent passage of Moroccan vessels through the waters off Ceuta or Melilla, acting now without requiring higher authorisation.

item.title: Shopkeepers defend their livelihood from masked looters during the French riots
item.description: Shopkeepers in several French cities tried to defend their businesses from looters during Saturday’s unrest, with confrontations leaving stores damaged and owners distressed.

item.title: Marine Le Pen warns of 'threat to democracy' and blasts 'exhausted Macronist power'
item.description: The far-right candidate for the 2027 presidential election speaks out the day after a day of riots that left France reeling, just as looting resumed in Paris.

item.title: Magyar links French riots to migration, says ‘shocking scenes’ justify hard line
item.description: Hungary’s Péter Magyar said riots in France justified his tough migration stance, echoed by Poland’s Donald Tusk. Left-wing critics accused him of exploiting the unrest, despite most protesters being French nationals.

item.title: Southern Valencia coast on alert as storm Adam may dump 300 mm of rain in 12 hours
item.description: The peak of this new DANA will come between Sunday and Monday, bringing heavy rain to Ibiza and Formentera and also to Alicante, Murcia and Almeria.

item.title: France: Paris, Lyon and Marseille count the cost after violent protests
item.description: Streets littered with broken glass, burnt bicycles and debris greeted residents in France on Sunday 18 October, following demonstrations that left extensive damage across Paris, Lyon and Marseille.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV after his hospital stay: "I feel closer to those who suffer illness"
item.description: Discharged on Saturday after surgery for a malignant tumour in his right lung, Pope Leo led the Angelus from the Apostolic Palace and thanked doctors, saying he will gradually resume duties.

item.title: Russia: Huge flames and smoke rise over St Petersburg after drone strikes
item.description: Huge plumes of black smoke billowed over St Petersburg, Russia’s second-largest city, on Sunday, 18 October, as a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack sparked fires at industrial and logistics facilities. Russian officials said 126 drones had been intercepted in the surrounding region.

item.title: Rubio arrives in Samarkand as Washington seeks closer ties with Central Asia
item.description: The US secretary of state will meet the foreign ministers of five Central Asian countries on Monday under the C5+1 format. Trade, investment, critical minerals and security are expected to feature in discussions, while more than 200 American business executives accompany the visit.

item.title: Check your wallet: some 2-euro coins are worth far more
item.description: They may say two euros, but collectors sometimes pay many times that amount: rare editions and striking minting errors can turn small change into sought-after treasures.

item.title: Cost-of-living protests: 50 detained in Milan, clashes in Turin and Bologna
item.description: Dozens of people were detained in Milan after clashes with the police during protests sparked by a march against the economic crisis. Tension was also reported in Turin and Bologna, with several demonstrators injured.

item.title: Businesses and shopkeepers pick up the pieces after protests in France spiral into looting
item.description: On Sunday morning, broken glass and litter filled the streets as Parisians emerged from their apartment blocks after a day of chaos across France.

item.title: Ukrainian forces strike St Petersburg and Leningrad region
item.description: It comes as Zelenskyy said Russian forces had targeted Ukraine's energy sector in strikes on four regions on Saturday night. He said attacks on residential buildings had also left two people dead and 12 others reportedly injured.

item.title: Burnt bicycles, smashed windows and looted shops: Trail of destruction across Paris
item.description: Burnt bicycles, smashed shopfronts and debris-filled streets mark the aftermath of Saturday’s protests in Paris, as cleanup crews begin clearing the damage.

item.title: Lyon wakes up to scenes of destruction after violent protests
item.description: Lyon is clearing up after a day of unrest, looting and vandalism during nationwide protests over the cost of living.

item.title: Off the Record: Trump blames Zelenskyy to cover up his own mess in a dramatic week for Ukraine
item.description: In her weekly newsletter, Euronews’ Europe editor Maria Tadeo debriefs the zeitgeist from Brussels. This week, she argues that Trump is scapegoating Zelenskyy for political reasons ahead of the US midterm elections.

item.title: Looting and buildings ablaze: France's violent Saturday protests in 10 pictures
item.description: Addressing the protests in a post on social media on Saturday evening, French President Emmanuel Macron said there was "no place for violence" in France.

item.title: France reels after cost-of-living protests see widespread violence
item.description: The French government has said around 1,200 arrests were made across France in relation to Saturday's events and that 150 police officers and gendarmes were injured over the course of the day.

item.title: Lisbon named Europe's best city and cruise destination for 2026
item.description: Lisbon has reclaimed its shine on Europe's tourism map, earning two titles at the World Travel Awards Europe 2026, presented on Saturday in Montenegro's Bay of Kotor.

item.title: Possible drone explosion in northern Lithuania near Latvian border
item.description: The incident is the latest in a growing series of drone incursions and incidents along NATO's eastern flank, many of which are believed to be spillover from Russia's war in Ukraine.

item.title: Four Canadian service members killed, dozens injured in fire at Alberta military base
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney described the incident as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada’s military on domestic soil.

item.title: Spire collapses at historic Limoges town hall amid violent protests across France
item.description: Major protests taking place across France on Saturday turned violent in a number of parts of the country as demonstrators clashed with police. Authorities said around 550,000 people took part in the protests nationwide.

item.title: Look, no hands: Euronews rode driverless in Europe's first robotaxi in Zagreb
item.description: The US firm’s robotaxi service is up and running in Zagreb in partnership with local company Verne and Chinese AI firm Pony.ai, a partnership that plans to expand across Europe. Euronews got to see how it works firsthand in Croatia.

item.title: Leisure out of reach for one in eight people in the EU: Where is the problem biggest?
item.description: From sport to cinema trips, regular leisure activities are out of reach for around 46 million people in the EU. Income helps explain the gap between countries, but it does not tell the whole story.

item.title: ‘Every sunny surface’ is being put to work. Europeans transforming their homes with solar driveways
item.description: “Every sunny surface we put to work brings Europe closer to an energy system that is cheaper, more secure and owned by the people it serves.”

item.title: Tee off in Europe’s most underrated golf holiday destinations
item.description: If you’re looking to book a European golfing holiday away from the traditional hotspots, then pack your clubs and head to underrated destinations like Varna on Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast, Gimsøya in Norway or Costa Navarino in Greece.
